newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares inch up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares inch up in quiet trade.

text.p: Cement, milling and housing shares featured in quiet trade on the Egyptian stock market on Wednesday as prices continued to inch up, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority share index rose 0.29 points to 241.05. Turnover was 51.8 million pounds ($15.2 million).
Cairo Housing and Development rose 7.94 percent, the highest net change, to close at 13.60 pounds.
"The housing sector has picked up again. The mill sector as a whole is doing well and cement is good," said one broker.

"The market is doing very well. People are willing to pay a premium now, but a lot of the eagerness has not translated into buying because there is still some blockage from the clearing and settling system."
Cements and mills were high on the turnover list.
Suez Cement turnover was 4.3 million, but its share fell 0.11 to 48.99 pounds. Amriyah Cement was steady at 58 pounds while 3.8 million changed hands.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 1.60 pounds to 51, and East Delta Flour Mills rose 1.11 to 40.50 pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 360.31 points from 360.89 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 170.12 from 169.65 points.
